messages:
ashok: Heads-up — planning a short maintenance micro-window for rack r12 (az3) tomorrow 03:00-03:20 UTC. We're doing NIC firmware soft-swap + safe reboot on the top-of-rack to resolve intermittent packet drops. Expected impact: single-cohort throughput dip for ~5-12m while traffic drains.

lina: Is this going to affect Dedicated pools or just hosted? any cross-region failover tests?

ashok: Primarily hosted edge pool in az3. We'll shift new incoming requests to az2 standby, and trigger graceful handoff for long-running streams. No Dedicated capacity will be drained unless nodes are colocated in the same rack (small handful).

ben-ops: Cost question — if we spill traffic to az2 standby burst, do we expect any charge bump on reserved capacity? we should flag finance for potential short-term egress increase.

kai: Quick runbook draft: 1) disable autoscale for affected pool 02:50, 2) set route weight az3->az2 to 10% then 100% using route-control, 3) cordon nodes in r12, 4) drain, 5) soft-restart NIC fw, 6) uncordon and reintroduce. Commands: ```route-control set-weight --from az3 --to az2 100; kubectl cordon node/r12-n{01..04}; kubectl drain node/r12-n01 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data```

infra-bot: Scheduled maintenance created: ID mnt-20240610-r12. Notifying oncall and posting to incident channel.

ashok: We'll do staggered drains by node every 3 minutes to avoid large KV cache cold starts. Plan to pre-warm by issuing a small primer load to the recovered nodes before flipping 100% traffic back.

lina: How are we avoiding long tail latency for streaming connections? can we gracefully rely on fallback model variant in the short window?

kai: Good call — add model-variant fallback in the routing policy for streams. Policy snippet: `if latency>300ms -> route to model-small-1` for the 20m window. Also we will lower max-connections-per-node to force quick handoff.

ben-ops: I'll ping finance and set a $ limit alarm for egress spike, and note this in the customer advisory if costs may materialize.

sre-oncall: I'll be on rotation during the window. If we see >2% error rate or token latency >500ms for 5m, we roll back route weight to az3 and re-evaluate.

ashok: Metrics to watch: p95 token latency, request error rate, active stream handoffs, kv-cache hit ratio. Dashboard: infra/r12-maint (will share link).

kai: Minor tweak — do NIC fw soft-swap with keepalive 30s to avoid BGP session churn. If BGP drops, infra-bot auto-fails to read-only route.

lina: I'll prepare a short customer note: 1 sentence + expected window + mitigation + who to contact. Minimal noise.

ashok: Thanks team. Final check-in at 02:30 UTC tomorrow in this thread. If anyone wants to add rollback steps or runbook bits now, please paste below.

ben-ops: Rollback add: restore route-control weights to previous snapshot and re-enable autoscale; revert firmware if repeated failures >1 node.

kai: Added a quick `kv-prime` job to warm caches: `jobs/kv-prime --target r12-n{01..04} --sample 1000`. Will run immediately after each node joins.

infra-bot: Reminder scheduled 30 minutes before maintenance: mnt-20240610-r12 (will post to #incidents and #customer-comm).
